faqs.a: An 8-digit HEX like #4f46e580 carries an alpha (opacity) channel in its last two digits. 80 in hex is 128 in decimal, and 128/255 = 0.50, so the color is 50% opaque.

For screens, HEX and RGB are identical in meaning — #ff0000 and rgb(255, 0, 0) are the same color. Use HEX for compactness in CSS, RGB when you need to read or compute channels, and RGBA when transparency is involved.
faqs.q: Should I use HEX or RGB in my CSS?

faqs.a: HSL (hue, saturation, lightness) matches how humans think about color: pick a hue, then adjust vividness and brightness. RGB matches how screens emit light. Converting between them is pure math with no information loss.
faqs.q: What is the difference between RGB and HSL?

faqs.a: CMYK is for print, where ink is subtracted from white paper instead of light added to a dark screen. The conversion here is the standard naive formula — real print shops use color profiles that may shift values slightly.
faqs.q: Why does the CMYK value differ from my print shop's?

faqs.a: Yes — type values like hsl(243, 75%, 59%) or hsla(243, 75%, 59%, 0.5). Hue accepts negative numbers and wraps around 360 degrees.
faqs.q: Can I paste an HSL value as input?

color-code-converter.formula:
HEX to RGB: split the 6 digits into three pairs, each pair is one channel in base 16
RGB to HSL: standard conversion via max/min channel and lightness
HSL to RGB: chroma C = (1 - |2L - 1|) x S, then sector math on H/60
RGB to CMYK: K = 1 - max(R,G,B); C = (max - R)/max, and so on

3-digit HEX (#fff) is shorthand for the 6-digit form (#ffffff).
8-digit HEX adds an alpha channel: the last two digits are opacity.
HSL hue wraps around 360 degrees, so -30 degrees equals 330 degrees.
All conversions are lossless except rounding to whole numbers.
